title: The engine verbs
intro: Twenty verbs that carry most Spanish sentences. Nearly all are irregular, which is exactly why they are worth memorising as forms rather than as rules. Where a verb has several meanings, each one gets its own sentence, labelled.

entries.en: to be — identity, origin, essence, time
entries.note: What something fundamentally is. Pairs with nouns, professions, nationalities and the clock.

entries.en: to be — location, condition, mood
entries.note: Where something is and how it is right now. A condition that could change tomorrow takes estar.

entries.en: there is, there are; to have (helper verb)
entries.note: As hay it never changes for plural. As he/has/ha it builds the perfect tense.

ex.es: Hay mucha gente en la calle.
ex.en: There are a lot of people in the street.

entries.en: to have, to own; to be (age, hunger, cold)
entries.note: Spanish uses tener where English uses be for bodily states.

entries.en: to do; to make; (weather) to be

ex.en: What are you doing on Sunday?

ex.es: Mi abuela hace un pan excelente.

entries.en: to go
entries.note: ir a + infinitive is the everyday future: voy a llamar = I'm going to call.

ex.en: We go to the market early.
I'm going to call you tonight.

entries.en: to come

ex.en: The train is coming in full.

entries.en: to be able to, can; may, to be allowed
to want; to love (a person)
entries.note: Te quiero is what you say to family, friends and partners. Te amo is heavier and rarer.

ex.en: I want a coffee without sugar.

entries.en: to know (a fact); to know how to; to taste (of)
entries.note: Facts and skills. Compare conocer, which is knowing by acquaintance.

ex.en: I don't know his last name.

entries.en: to know (a person, a place); to meet for the first time
entries.note: You conoces a city; you sabes its population.

entries.en: to say, to tell

ex.en: They say it's going to rain.

entries.en: to see; to watch
entries.note: Nos vemos — literally we see each other — is the standard see you later.

ex.es: Desde aquí se ve el mar.
ex.en: You can see the sea from here.
We watch a film on Fridays.

entries.en: to give; to face, to look onto

ex.en: The window looks onto the courtyard.

entries.en: to put, to place; to turn on; (ponerse) to put on, to become

ex.es: Pon el plato en la mesa.
ex.en: Put the plate on the table.

ex.es: Se puso el abrigo y salió.
ex.en: He put on his coat and left.

ex.es: Se puso nervioso antes del examen.
ex.en: He got nervous before the exam.

entries.en: must, ought to; to owe
entries.note: debe = must. debe de = probably. One preposition separates obligation from guesswork.

entries.en: to carry, to take along; to wear; to have spent (time)

ex.es: Lleva los libros a la oficina.
ex.en: Take the books to the office.

entries.en: to arrive; to reach; to manage to

ex.es: El vuelo llega a las seis.
El agua llegó hasta la puerta.

ex.en: I never got to know him.

entries.en: to return, to go back; volver a + inf., to do again

ex.en: I'll be back in five minutes.

entries.en: to remain, to be left; to arrange to meet; (quedarse) to stay

ex.en: We agreed to meet on Thursday.

ex.es: Me quedé en casa todo el día.
